summary: Phase 4 focused close-out validation (credit-conscious, per scope). Re-ran backend/tests/test_phase4.py: 23 passed, 1 skipped (env-dependent) - confirms determinism fix in commit_pipeline.py holds. Live-verified via curl on real runs: (1) Timeline/milestones - /timeline is chronological (descending, newest-first) and byte-identical on re-fetch; /milestones only ever emitted approved types (first_shelter, shelter_completed, first_major_discovery, first_death) across all sessions observed. (2) Load/continue - GET /runs/{id} and /state report identical last_state_hash/current_tick; replay/verify passes before and after simulated 'reload+continue'. (3) Causal/provenance/tile-history - all three endpoints stable across repeated calls (byte-identical diffs), tile history returns bounded per-tile projections with correct disclaimer text, and provenance.relationships_note correctly says 'not applicable to this world model' rather than fabricating a relationship. (4) Death doctrine - kill_entity intervention correctly sets alive=false/current_goal=DEAD, freezes position, appears in timeline+milestones (first_death), dead entity produces ZERO further events after the kill tick (verified via timeline?entity_id filter), and total entity count only grows (shelters/new entities) never shrinks/respawns. (5) Hunt->carcass->meat food chain - COULD NOT BE OBSERVED. Ran ~2900 ticks across 2 dedicated runs with repeated max hunger boosts on all 6 persons; queried the full MongoDB accepted_events collection (190,539 events across ALL runs created this session + prior sessions/pytest runs) - zero 'hunt_strike' events, zero carcass entities, zero events with 'hunt' in explanation, ever. Code-level analysis of people_utility.py's HUNT utility scoring shows HUNT carries a large fixed risk penalty (risk*70 = -350 day / -1050 night) plus a 0.7x severity discount that are subtracted unconditionally even when the term is otherwise capped - the UI Utility Breakdown panel (screenshot-verified) confirms HUNT scores are typically deeply negative or losing to SEEK_FOOD/EXPLORE/WANDER in every observed situation. It is unclear from black-box testing alone whether HUNT is merely very rare (needs a hungry person + zero known food + an animal within VISION_RADIUS=4 simultaneously) or effectively unreachable due to scoring - flagging as inconclusive/high-priority for a targeted unit-level check rather than declaring it broken. Frontend smoke: App loads, WorldCanvas renders (canvas grid with correct entity colors), LoadRunModal lists 200+ runs and loads a selected one correctly, TimelineTab renders chronological events with milestone badges, TileInspector shows correct empty-tile projection with doctrine disclaimer text, EntityInspector's deeper panels (Utility Breakdown, Decision Explanation, Causal Chain, Provenance) are all accurate and match backend data (kill_entity tick=16 correctly shown).

minor.issue: Zero hunt_strike/carcass events found across 190,539 accepted_events in the entire DB (multiple long test runs + boosted hunger). HUNT candidate's fixed risk penalty (-350/-1050) and 0.7x severity discount may make it practically unreachable in normal play, or it may just require very specific rare conditions (no known food AND animal within VISION_RADIUS=4 simultaneously) not hit in ~2900 stepped ticks. Recommend a direct unit-level test calling decide()/people_planning HUNT path with a synthetic hungry-person-adjacent-to-animal-no-known-food state to confirm HUNT can ever win and complete end-to-end (travel->hunt_strike->carcass->gather meat into food_inventory).

ui_bugs.issue: The top-level 'Death Record' box reads entity.death_cause / entity.death_tick which DO NOT EXIST on the raw entity object returned by the API (always renders 'unknown' / '-' for every dead person/animal, including the kill_entity case tested). The CORRECT death cause/tick data does exist and IS displayed correctly further down the same panel via the Causal Chain ('t=16 kill_entity - external intervention...') and Provenance ('death: {tick:16, event_id, explanation}') sections - so the bug is cosmetic/duplicative but should be fixed to read from provenance.death or causal.entity's lifecycle_diagnostics instead of nonexistent fields.

action_items: Fix EntityInspector.jsx 'Death Record' box to source cause/tick from provenance/causal death data instead of non-existent entity.death_cause/entity.death_tick fields

Investigate whether HUNT is ever practically reachable given its scoring penalties - confirm via a targeted unit test (bypass the need for organic emergent conditions) that the full hunt_strike -> carcass -> gather-meat-into-food_inventory chain executes correctly end-to-end at least once
critical_code_review_comments: commit_pipeline.py determinism fix (removing 'seq' from content_hash) verified correct: TestDeliberateResourceContention::test_proposal_arrival_order_does_not_affect_outcome passes.

history_service.py correctly remains read-only (verified via TestReplayDoctrineNotBypassedByHistory tests, and via my own manual re-fetch stability checks on /timeline, /entities/.../causal, /entities/.../provenance, /tiles/.../history - all byte-identical across repeated calls).

lifecycle_domain.py is a clean, side-effect-free proposal-only domain (LifecycleDomain has zero instance state per test), correctly runs at environment-phase priority 1 so a person's death commits before their own agent-phase action in the same tick.

interventions.py's kill_entity correctly goes through the same commit pipeline as any domain proposal (has a precondition, produces a real accepted_event) rather than special-casing a direct DB write - matches the 'paired model' doctrine.

people_utility.py's HUNT scoring formula subtracts risk*70 unconditionally (even when availability=0 and need_term is already capped at 45), which seems like an oversight worth a second look even if not confirmed broken - it makes HUNT's floor score very negative in all cases, possibly beyond what's intended by the '0.7x discount, slower/riskier than foraging' design comment.

success_rate.backend: ~96% (23/24 test_phase4.py tests pass, 1 environment-dependent skip; all manually-verified endpoints in the 5 scoped areas behave correctly except the unverified hunt food-chain)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested smoke flows (load run, WorldCanvas, TimelineTab, TileInspector, EntityInspector causal/provenance panels) work correctly; 1 minor cosmetic display bug found

No cleanup performed; consistent with prior sessions' practice (no cleanup endpoint exists, single-user local sandbox tool).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 5 requested Phase 4 areas were exercised except the hunt->carcass->meat chain, which could not be organically triggered within budget (~2900 ticks, max hunger boosts) and has ZERO occurrences in the entire 190k-event MongoDB history across this and prior sessions. This is either a very rare emergent condition or a scoring-design issue in people_utility.py's HUNT candidate (large unconditional risk penalty). If picking this up: the fastest way to confirm/deny is a backend unit test that directly constructs a person entity with hunger>=900, empty known_trees, and a living non-fleeing animal at distance<=1 within a hand-built ActivationFrame, then asserts HUNT proposals reach hunt_strike and a carcass entity + food_inventory increment - this avoids depending on organic emergence. Also fix the EntityInspector Death Record cosmetic bug (reads nonexistent entity.death_cause/death_tick).
rca_of_the_issue: EntityInspector Death Record bug: frontend code was written assuming the backend would attach death_cause/death_tick directly onto the entity document, but the actual backend design (correctly, per doctrine) keeps death provenance derived/projected via history_service (causal/provenance endpoints) rather than mutating the entity with those fields - a frontend/backend contract mismatch, not a backend bug. Hunt food-chain: inconclusive - either genuinely rare given map size (20x20), VISION_RADIUS=4, and animal flee behavior, or the risk*70 unconditional penalty in the HUNT utility term makes it lose to WANDER/EXPLORE/SEEK_FOOD in effectively all real game states; requires a controlled unit test to distinguish these two hypotheses.
